expectations.text: Explains informative references as crosswalks mapping CSF 2.0 outcomes (functions/categories/subcategories) to other standards and resources
expectations.evidence: they tell you which sections of other standards and frameworks (ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-53, COBIT, CIS...) are relevant to a given CSF subcategory

expectations.text: Points to NIST SP 1347, the CSF 2.0 Informative References Quick-Start Guide, finalized August 2026
expectations.evidence: No mention of NIST SP 1347 or the August 2026 Informative References Quick-Start Guide

expectations.text: Mentions the CSF 2.0 Reference Tool for browsing/exporting reference data
expectations.evidence: NIST maintains these mappings in the CSF Reference Tool / NIST Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool (CPRT), an online, machine-readable repository

expectations.text: Mentions the OLIR (Online Informative References) program as the mechanism behind the mappings
expectations.evidence: OLIR (Online Informative References) program never mentioned

expectations.text: Demonstrates a concrete mapping use: e.g., ISO 27001/SP 800-53/CIS Controls mapped against CSF subcategories for gap or evidence reuse
expectations.evidence: For PR.AA-01, you'd typically see references into ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A (e.g., A.5.16, A.8.5), NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (e.g., IA-2, IA-4, IA-5)
